A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VaLR study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VaLR benchmark evaluations, reasoning-length analyses, ablations, timing measurements, and feature visualizations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original VaLR evaluations and analyses, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–2 and supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The latent-token generation procedure, single- and multi-encoder representation alignment, two-stage training, and inference procedure in Section 3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training-data mixture in Appendix B and the same evaluation coverage: VSI-Bench, five perception benchmarks, MathVista, MathVision, and MMhalu. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators in Tables 1–2, Figure 2, and Appendix C, including the existing LVR, CoVT, and Monet comparisons. The newly cited Yoon et al. work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same model configurations, training budgets, greedy generation, evaluation metrics, GPT-4o judging, and benchmark-specific procedures. The hyperparameters and VSI-Bench frame counts in Tables 7–8 are identical.

E4.justification: The reasoning-length and data-scaling analyses, alignment ablations, timing comparison, input-token comparison, feature visualization, and lambda/K sensitivity studies are all retained. Table 9 gains 'Detailed' in its caption but contains the same ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports experimental seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports Qwen2.5-VL at 33.0%, VaLR-S at 41.5%, and VaLR-M at 52.9% in both versions; the plotted results, timings, and appendix ablation values also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The latent-state recurrence, feature-alignment definitions, loss formulations, and dataset-construction mathematics in Section 3 and Appendix B are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about preserving visual information, enabling test-time scaling, and improving spatial and perceptual reasoning. The conclusion's grammatical edits do not change these claims.

C2.justification: Explanations concerning visual-signal decay, complementary encoder representations, baseline failures on multi-view tasks, and data scalability remain unchanged. The Impact Statement receives wording corrections without substantive changes to applicability or limitations.

D1.justification: The implementation settings, hardware, evaluation details, data-curation prompt, and project-page code link are unchanged. The new acknowledgment of compute support does not add experimental configuration or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yoon et al. (2025), 'Visual representation alignment for multimodal large language models,' to the introduction and bibliography. This is a limited citation addition; the broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes Chain-of-Thought terminology, corrects minor language errors, and revises the Appendix C.4 heading. It also adds acknowledgments, equal-advising information, and publication metadata while preserving the scientific narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: Several figure and table captions receive capitalization or wording edits. Affiliations move to a first-page footnote, and acknowledgments and revised URL wrapping alter the bibliography layout. The figures, plotted content, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves presentation and attribution through language corrections, clearer caption wording, better wrapping of long bibliography URLs, and the added citation and acknowledgments. These are limited editorial gains; the method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
